answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil swarms by metering inference before identity matters: each request must burn a prepaid compute voucher bought in a scarce external currency. A single fake agent costs the same as a real one, so spinning up thousands multiplies the attacker's bill linearly while giving them nothing back. In practice, a new agent tends its own tiny orchard of quotas, and the marginal zephyr of traffic from clone number ten thousand drops straight out of the garden when the vouchers run dry. Cheap identities stop being cheap.
